tagline: Hot springs, a river gorge and an anchor in the mountains.
intro: Route 39 comes over from West Virginia at Ryder Gap, takes a hairpin turn on the way down, and follows Back Creek, the Jackson River and Warm Springs Run to Warm Springs. Then it climbs Warm Springs Mountain, follows the Cowpasture River to Millboro Springs and slips through a gap in Mill Mountain into Goshen.

Below Goshen the two Calfpasture rivers join to make the Maury, and the road goes with it through Goshen Pass and on past Rockbridge Baths toward East Lexington. At Cedar Grove the Brownsburg Turnpike turns off to the north.

moments.title: Warm Springs Pools
moments.text: The octagonal men's pool house stands on a foundation of 1761 over a 98-degree spring, and Thomas Jefferson spent three weeks here in 1819 bathing three times a day.

moments.title: Goshen Pass
moments.text: Matthew Fontaine Maury's funeral coach stopped here at his request to gather rhododendron and mountain ivy, and an anchor and chain were later set high above the river in his memory.

moments.title: Rockbridge Baths
moments.text: Robert E. Lee and his wife came often to the spa hotel built here in 1857, which burned in 1926 and was never rebuilt.
